@zWORMzGaming  You absolutely cannot get official FSR 4 support for Cyberpunk, because CDPR chose to use FSR 3.0 that is baked in the game files. Unless CDPR upgrades their game themselves specifically with 3.1 or 4.0, AMD can't do anything, because you need a file swap for it to work.

What you can do as a owner of 9000-series card, and should do, is to use Optiscaler mod to insert FSR 4 in game. It's pretty easy to install and use and works well. Copy-paste contents of the archive in game exe folder and run the install bat, and then enable it with ingame menu that opens with "insert key".

OS works well in BG3 as well.

Also, there is a great mod that enables basic path-tracing for lot more GPU's for Cyberpunk. It's called "Ultra+" and running it in RT+PT mode.

text:
To override FSR to FSR4 the game needs to at least use FSR3.1 because with 3.1 they introduced the use of FSR in dll form which then can be overriden in the driver. While some devs did implement FSR3 or even 2 using dll, but those were not standardized thus replacing it will be a bit more trickier. Also technically it is possible to replace non dll FSR implementation but the implication will be similar to when AMD tried to implement Antilag+ which in some games ended up tripping anticheat. Heck, even doing dll override can potentially trip anticheat (some EA games have been reported of behaving like that).
Basically don't expect non FSR3.1 to get FSR4 support unless the devs actually update their FSR version to 3.1. Right now your best bet of using FSR4 in more titles is using Optiscaler, which can replace DLSS/XeSS/FSR with FSR4.
Also from my experience it seems if you use DLSS or XeSS as the base for FSR4 it can look better than if you use FSR2 or 3 as the base. Some devs did a bad job at implementing FSR that if you use FSR2/3 as the base and replace that with FSR4, it ended up looking not great vs when using XeSS or DLSS and replace that with FSR4. I noticed this in CP2077 which as we all know by know, it has a terrible FSR implementation. I wouldn't be surprised if Stalker and Oblivion FSR4 ended up looking better if you can hook FSR4 to their DLSS/XeSS.
Also currently FSR4 doesn't support Vulkan thus you can't use it in a game like Indiana Jones.

Regarding performance, because 9070 is relatively more power limited than 9070XT (basically 9070 is close to its peak efficiency vs 9070XT) it should respond better to overclocking. The performance increase (%) on 9070 should be higher than on 9070XT.

Lastly, I wouldn't recommend people to buy 12GB GPU at $500 and up unless you're the type to upgrade GPU every 1 or 2 years. It should be good enough if you're willing to lower texture quality, but honestly in the future there will be more games where technically 5070 is still powerful enough in terms of compute to just run at max settings but you probably need to lower some settings that can consume VRAM like texture and RT. Right now there are already some games like that. I would consider recommending 5070 if it is closer to $400 than to $500.
